attributes.scope: MWCC GC 1.2.5, cflags_demo family (-Cpp_exceptions on, -O4 -inline auto). Population measured: 26 copy sites in one function, 18 u64 and 8 struct, both directions probed. Practical use: on a PS2-derived TU, a GS privileged-register write list is u64 by nature and a per-field display-environment record is not, so the store order is readable evidence for which reconstruction is faithful.

falsifier: An 8-byte copy through `*(u64*)` under these cflags that stores +0 before +4, or a two-u32 struct copy that stores +4 first. Re-check with `python tools/gdl/fnasm.py game/pb/pb_frame.c pbFrameMode 0xad0:0xb00 --diff` (u64 group) beside `... 0x5a0:0x5c4 --diff` (struct group); if the two groups stop disagreeing in store order after an unrelated edit, the type is not the discriminant.
subject: compiler:mwcc-gc-1.2.5
value: An 8-byte copy through a 4-aligned pointer cast emits two lwz and two stw either way, but the STORE ORDER names the source type: `*(u64*)d = *(u64*)s;` loads +0 then +4 and stores +4 BEFORE +0, while a two-u32 struct copy `*(P8*)d = *(P8*)s;` stores +0 then +4 in field order. The load order is the same (+0 then +4) in both, so the discriminant is the store pair alone, and it also flips which of the two scratch registers holds which half — which is why the row reads as a wrong-displacement bug in an fndiff IMMEDIATE census and is not one. Measured on pbFrameMode (pb_frame.c) at 9cb7d2ab7, which contains BOTH forms 40 instructions apart: the tpl-sourced GS-register copies are u64 (`@0xad4 lwz r7,0(r3)` / `@0xadc lwz r8,4(r3)` / `@0xae8 stw r8,36(r6)` / `@0xaec stw r7,32(r6)`), the env-sourced display-environment copies are two-u32 structs (`@0x5a4 lwz r8,0(r7)` / `@0x5a8 lwz r0,4(r7)` / `@0x5ac stw r8,448(r6)` / `@0x5b0 stw r0,452(r6)`). Retyping all 26 sites to u64 took real 391 -> 317; putting the 8 env sites back to the struct form took it to 253, and each direction was wrong for the other group by exactly its own row count.
